blocks.text: If you only have a day in Bondi and want the honest local shortlist, here it is: swim between the flags, walk the coastal path to Bronte, and eat your way along Campbell Parade. That trio is the heart of the place, but there's a lot more - 34 of my favourite things to do in Bondi, from the obvious icons to the corners most visitors walk straight past.

items.label: Getting here
items.value: Bus from Bondi Junction rail (check Transport for NSW)

items.label: Cost
items.value: Most of this list is free

blocks.text: The big three you can't skip

Start with the water. Bondi is patrolled, and the most important rule I give anyone is to swim between the red-and-yellow flags - the surf here has rips, and the flags mark where the lifeguards want you. If the ocean's too wild, the Bondi Icebergs ocean pool at the south end is the postcard shot for a reason, and there's a free tidal pool at the north end too.

items: Swim between the flags on the main beach
Do the Bondi to Bronte coastal walk (around 2.5km of clifftop path)
Take a surf lesson with one of the beachfront surf schools
Cool off in the Icebergs ocean pool or the free north-end pool
Walk the full promenade and take in the ever-changing street art on the sea wall

blocks.text: Do the coastal walk early - before about 8am in summer - and you'll have the clifftops and the light almost to yourself, well before the crowds and parking headaches arrive.

blocks.title: Respect the surf
blocks.text: Bondi's rips are real and they catch strong swimmers out. Always check conditions and swim between the flags - read the current beach report on Surf Life Saving's Beachsafe first.

Bondi isn't only sand. The Bondi Pavilion, right on the beach, reopened after a big restoration and now runs exhibitions, workshops and live performance - check the Waverley Council programme for what's on. On weekends the Bondi Markets take over Bondi Beach Public School on Campbell Parade: the Sunday market leans into fashion, art and vintage, with a Saturday farmers' market for produce and coffee. Confirm current days and hours on the Bondi Markets site first.

items: Browse the weekend Bondi Markets at Bondi Beach Public School
Catch an exhibition or workshop at the Bondi Pavilion
Spread a picnic or kick a ball on Bondi Park above the sand
Let the kids loose on the beachside playground
Wander the quiet, dramatic clifftop graves of Waverley Cemetery
Learn the story of surf rescue at the Bondi Surf Bathers' Life Saving Club
Detour up to Ben Buckler for the clifftop views over the whole bay

stops.title: Coastal walk + swim
stops.detail: Walk Bondi to Bronte, then double back for a swim between the flags.

stops.title: Markets + lunch
stops.detail: Graze the weekend markets, then grab lunch along Campbell Parade or Hall Street.

stops.title: Pavilion + pool
stops.detail: See what's on at the Pavilion and finish with a dip at the Icebergs pool.

blocks.text: Where I eat, drink and watch the world go by

Half the fun of Bondi is grazing. [Messina](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/gelato-messina-bondi) does some of Sydney's best gelato, the [North Bondi RSL](/bondi-eat-and-drink/venues/north-bondi-rsl) serves an honest meal with a genuinely million-dollar view, and there are enough cafés, pubs and rooftop bars around Hall Street to keep you busy for days - I keep a running guide to [where to eat and drink in Bondi](/bondi-eat-and-drink) if you want the full picture. And never underestimate the free entertainment: grab a promenade bench and people-watch - Bondi delivers a parade like nowhere else in Sydney.

items: Grab gelato from Messina
Eat with a view at North Bondi RSL
Sink a beer at one of the local pubs or rooftop bars
Have a long brunch at a Bondi café
Take a whale-watching cruise in season (roughly May to November)
People-watch from a promenade bench
Go for a run in either direction along the coast
Catch summer extras like the open-air cinema when they're on

items.q: What are the best free things to do in Bondi?
items.a: Most of Bondi's best is free: swimming between the flags, the coastal walk to Bronte, the promenade and sea-wall art, Bondi Park, Waverley Cemetery, the weekend markets, and people-watching. You only pay for food, drinks, classes and tours.

items.q: How long should I spend at Bondi Beach?
items.a: A half-day covers the essentials - a swim, the coastal walk and lunch. To add the markets, the Pavilion, a surf lesson and a long dinner, give yourself a full day or more.

items.q: Is Bondi Beach safe for swimming?
items.a: It's patrolled and lifeguarded but does have rips. Swim between the red-and-yellow flags, check conditions on Surf Life Saving's Beachsafe, and if the surf's too big, use the ocean pools.

items.q: How do I get to Bondi Beach without a car?
items.a: The simplest way is the train to Bondi Junction, then a bus to the beach. Parking near the sand is limited and slow on weekends, so public transport is usually easier - check Transport for NSW for routes and times.

items.q: When can I see whales at Bondi?
items.a: Whale migration off Sydney runs roughly from May to November. Boats depart from Sydney Harbour, and you can sometimes spot whales from the clifftops in season.

blocks.text: That's my Bondi in a nutshell - swim, walk, eat, repeat, with art and people-watching in between. Pick a few from this list, leave room to wander, and you'll find your own favourite corner of the beach.
